look_here_first: Start with the smooth leathery mature capsule and flower structure: stamens are usually included or barely extend beyond the tubular petals. Opposite palmately compound leaves confirm buckeye but not species; yellow-flowered var. flavescens means red color is not a universal species key.

taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Aesculus pavia L. with var. pavia and var. flavescens. Master Plant Pool row 24 (A. pavia var. pavia) is an infraspecific source concept represented by this species-level card, not a third species. Yellow-flowered var. flavescens is not to be mislabeled as var. pavia. Hybrid Aesculus × bushii can show intermediate traits.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous shrub to small tree, sometimes multistemmed.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, palmately compound with usually 5 (sometimes 7) serrate leaflets; leaf count overlaps A. glabra.
morphology_keys.flowers: Terminal panicles with relatively tubular unequal petals; stamens included to slightly exserted, approximately petal length. Typical flowers red, but accepted var. flavescens can be yellow.
morphology_keys.fruits: Smooth, rounded leathery capsule usually lacking the short prickles typical of A. glabra; large shiny brown seeds.
best_field_traits: stamens included or only slightly beyond petals
tubular flower profile and unequal petals

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. glabra generally has short-prickly/warty capsules and stamens strongly exserted (about twice petal length). A. × bushii may be intermediate. A. flava also has smooth fruits but differs in flower architecture and habit; use full reproductive key. Ungnadia has pinnate leaves and a three-valved capsule. Never use red flower color as the only diagnostic.
